-- True when `path` is relative and never climbs above its starting
-- directory, however the `..` and `.` segments are mixed.
stays_inside(path: str) -> bool =
  ex stays_inside("a.txt") == True
  ex stays_inside("sub/../a.txt") == True
  ex stays_inside("sub/./b/../a.txt") == True
  ex stays_inside("..") == False
  ex stays_inside("../notes/a.txt") == False
  ex stays_inside("/etc/passwd") == False
  ex stays_inside("sub/../../x") == False
  ex stays_inside("") == False
  if path.char_count() == 0
    return False
  let parts = path.split("/")
  if parts[0] == ""
    return False
  var depth = 0
  for seg in parts
    if seg == "" or seg == "."
      continue
    if seg == ".."
      depth -= 1
      if depth < 0
        return False
      continue
    depth += 1
  True

-- Text of the file at `path` inside `notes`, or "" when the path leaves
-- `notes`, or the file is missing or unreadable.
read_public(path: str) -> str uses fs =
  post stays_inside(path) or out == ""
  ex read_public("..") == ""
  ex read_public("/etc/passwd") == ""
  ex read_public("sub/../../x") == ""
  var text = ""
  if stays_inside(path)
    with fs = fs.sub("notes")
      text = fs.read(path) else ""
  text

test_stays_inside() =
  assert stays_inside("sub/../a.txt")
  assert not stays_inside("sub/../../x")
  assert not stays_inside("/abs")
